-- The queries of the notes, claimed by NoteQueries.  The schema's enum and domains are read as C# types of the project:
-- the enum as a C# enum that the data source maps, and each domain through the converters of its type.  The ids of the
-- accounts are AccountIds, read and sent through its converters: accounts.id and notes.account_id by the header's
-- -- column: markers.
-- type-override: public.note_kind = SqlSource.DatabaseTests.Postgres.EndToEnd.Types.NoteKind
-- type-override: public.email = SqlSource.DatabaseTests.Postgres.EndToEnd.Types.Email
-- type-override: public.note_ref = SqlSource.DatabaseTests.Postgres.EndToEnd.Types.NoteRef
-- column: accounts.id -> AccountId
-- column: notes.account_id -> AccountId

-- name: ListAccountNotes
-- summary: Every account with its notes, and an account with none once, with NULL for the note.
SELECT
    a.id,
    a.name,
    n.id AS note_id,
    n.account_id,
    n.kind,
    n.body
FROM accounts AS a
LEFT JOIN notes AS n ON n.account_id = a.id
ORDER BY a.id, n.id;

-- name: CountAccountNotes
-- summary: The number of notes of each account.
-- A count has no source column, so the column types do not reach it, and the marker gives it its type.
-- column: note_count -> NoteCount
SELECT
    a.id,
    count(n.id) AS note_count
FROM accounts AS a
LEFT JOIN notes AS n ON n.account_id = a.id
GROUP BY a.id
ORDER BY a.id;

-- name: GetAccountNoteCount -> one
-- summary: The number of notes of the account that an id names.
-- A parameter has no source column either: the marker gives it its C# type, and the database infers its type from the
-- column it is compared with.
-- param: @id -> AccountId
-- column: note_count -> NoteCount
SELECT
    a.id,
    count(n.id) AS note_count
FROM accounts AS a
LEFT JOIN notes AS n ON n.account_id = a.id
WHERE a.id = @id
GROUP BY a.id;

-- name: GetAccountNoteCountSync -> one
-- summary: GetAccountNoteCount, by a synchronous method, which sends and reads through the converters.
-- param: @id -> AccountId
-- column: note_count -> NoteCount
-- generator: method-type=sync
SELECT
    a.id,
    count(n.id) AS note_count
FROM accounts AS a
LEFT JOIN notes AS n ON n.account_id = a.id
WHERE a.id = @id
GROUP BY a.id;

-- name: ListDisplayNames
-- summary: The name of each account with each word capitalized.
-- column: display_name not null
-- initcap is never NULL for a name that is not, and the tool does not prove it, so the column would be nullable
-- without its marker.
SELECT
    a.id,
    initcap(a.name) AS display_name
FROM accounts AS a
ORDER BY a.id;

-- name: ListMarkedNames
-- summary: The names of the accounts, with their nullability set by the marks of their aliases.
-- As in ListDisplayNames, the column would be nullable without its mark.  A function that the tool proves, such as
-- upper, would leave the mark nothing to show.
SELECT
    a.id AS "id?",
    initcap(a.name) AS "initcap_name!"
FROM accounts AS a
ORDER BY a.id;

-- name: ListNoteKinds
-- summary: The kind of each note and the email of its account.
SELECT
    n.kind,
    a.email
FROM notes AS n
JOIN accounts AS a ON a.id = n.account_id
ORDER BY n.id;

-- name: ListNoteKindsForDapper
-- summary: ListNoteKinds again, at the output models, whose constant the Dapper tests run.
-- output: models
-- member-location: class
-- output-model: ListNoteKindsDto
SELECT
    n.kind,
    a.email
FROM notes AS n
JOIN accounts AS a ON a.id = n.account_id
ORDER BY n.id;

-- name: GetNoteByRef -> one
-- summary: The note that a ref names, with its ref.
-- A parameter compared with a column of a domain is described as the domain's base type, so the marker declares it as
-- the domain, which the type override gives the type NoteRef.
-- param: @ref public.note_ref
SELECT
    n.id,
    n.ref,
    n.body
FROM notes AS n
WHERE n.ref = @ref;

-- name: FindNotesByEmail
-- summary: The notes of the account that an email names, with each note's ref, which may be NULL.
-- param: @email public.email
SELECT
    n.id,
    n.ref,
    a.email
FROM notes AS n
JOIN accounts AS a ON a.id = n.account_id
WHERE a.email = @email
ORDER BY n.id;

-- name: StreamNoteAccounts
-- summary: The accounts that have notes, with the id of each as an AccountId, read through its converters.
-- collection-type: IAsyncEnumerable
SELECT DISTINCT account_id FROM notes
ORDER BY account_id;
